source.name: IELTS Writing Band Descriptors (Task 2), public version
source.note: Each band entry below is a paraphrased summary written by the team, not a verbatim copy of the official descriptors. Bands 0-2 are condensed into 'floor_rules'.

scoring_notes: Each criterion is scored as an integer 0-9. A response should fit the positive features of a band to receive it; negative features cap the band.
Estimated band for learning purposes only, not an official IELTS result.
Calibration range is band 4-8; results outside it are flagged out_of_calibration_range.

floor_rules.band_2: Content barely relates to the prompt, no position can be identified, almost no control of organisation, vocabulary or sentence forms.
floor_rules.band_1: 20 words or fewer, or content wholly unrelated to the prompt; no usable language.
floor_rules.band_0: Not attempted, not in English, or proven to be fully memorised.

CRIT_W_TR.name: Task Response
CRIT_W_TR.focus: Addresses every part of the prompt, takes a clear position, and develops relevant ideas with support.

bands.9: Prompt fully addressed and explored in depth; position is clear and fully developed; ideas are relevant, fully extended and well supported; lapses are extremely rare.
bands.8: Prompt addressed appropriately and sufficiently; position is clear and well developed; ideas are relevant and well extended and supported; only occasional omissions.
bands.7: Main parts of the prompt addressed; position is clear and developed; main ideas are extended and supported, but may over-generalise or lack focus and precision in support.
bands.6: Main parts addressed, some more fully than others; position is relevant but conclusions may be unclear, unjustified or repetitive; some ideas are underdeveloped or have weak or irrelevant support.
bands.5: Main parts only partly addressed; a position is stated but its development is not always clear; ideas are limited, thinly developed, with irrelevant detail or repetition.
bands.4: Prompt handled minimally or somewhat off to the side; position hard to find; main ideas unclear, irrelevant or unsupported; large parts may repeat.
bands.3: No part of the prompt adequately addressed or it was misunderstood; no relevant position; few ideas, irrelevant or undeveloped.

CRIT_W_CC.name: Coherence and Cohesion
CRIT_W_CC.focus: Logical organisation and progression, paragraphing, and accurate, natural use of linking and reference.

bands.9: Message followed effortlessly; cohesion rarely draws attention; lapses minimal; paragraphing handled skilfully.
bands.8: Message followed with ease; ideas logically sequenced and cohesion well managed; occasional lapses; paragraphing sufficient and appropriate.
bands.7: Clear logical organisation and progression with minor lapses; a range of cohesive devices, including reference and substitution, used flexibly but with some inaccuracy or over/under-use; paragraphing generally effective.
bands.6: Ideas generally coherent with clear overall progression; linking works to some effect but can be faulty or mechanical (misuse, overuse, omission); reference may lack clarity; paragraphing not always logical.
bands.5: Organisation visible but not wholly logical, progression may be lacking though some underlying coherence remains; ideas can be followed but sentences link poorly; limited or overused linkers; repetitive reference; paragraphing inadequate or missing.
bands.4: Ideas present but not arranged coherently, no clear progression; relationships between ideas unclear; only basic, possibly inaccurate or repetitive linkers; poor reference; paragraphing may be absent.
bands.3: No apparent logical organisation; ideas hard to relate; minimal linking that does not signal real relationships; reference hard to follow; paragraphing unhelpful.

CRIT_W_LR.name: Lexical Resource
CRIT_W_LR.focus: Range, precision and appropriacy of vocabulary, including collocation, word formation and spelling.

bands.9: Wide vocabulary used precisely, naturally and with sophisticated control; spelling and word-formation slips are extremely rare.
bands.8: Wide vocabulary used fluently and flexibly for precise meaning; skilful use of uncommon or idiomatic items, with occasional word-choice or collocation slips; occasional spelling or word-form errors with minimal impact.
bands.7: Vocabulary sufficient for some flexibility and precision; some use of less common or idiomatic items; awareness of style and collocation though inappropriate uses occur; only a few spelling or word-form errors.
bands.6: Vocabulary generally adequate; meaning generally clear despite restricted range or imprecise choices; risk-taking brings range but more inaccuracy; some spelling or word-form errors that do not impede understanding.
bands.5: Vocabulary limited but minimally adequate; simple words mostly accurate but little variation; frequent inappropriate choices, simplification and repetition; noticeable spelling or word-form errors that can strain the reader.
bands.4: Vocabulary limited, basic and repetitive, possibly inadequate for the task; may misuse memorised phrases or wording copied from the prompt; word-choice, word-form or spelling errors can impede meaning.
bands.3: Vocabulary inadequate (possibly because the essay is far too short); heavy reliance on the prompt or memorised language; errors in word choice and spelling predominate and may block meaning.

CRIT_W_GRA.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
CRIT_W_GRA.focus: Variety and control of sentence structures, grammatical accuracy and punctuation.

bands.9: Wide range of structures used with full flexibility and control; grammar and punctuation appropriate throughout; minor errors extremely rare.
bands.8: Wide range of structures used flexibly and accurately; most sentences error-free and punctuation well managed; occasional non-systematic errors with minimal impact.
bands.7: Variety of complex structures used with some flexibility and accuracy; grammar and punctuation generally well controlled with frequent error-free sentences; a few persistent errors that do not impede understanding.
bands.6: Mix of simple and complex sentences but limited flexibility; complex structures less accurate than simple ones; errors in grammar and punctuation occur but rarely impede understanding.
bands.5: Range of structures limited and repetitive; complex sentences attempted but usually faulty, simple sentences most accurate; frequent errors that can cause difficulty; punctuation may be faulty.
bands.4: Very limited range, mostly simple sentences with few subordinate clauses; some accurate structures but frequent errors that may impede meaning; punctuation often faulty.
bands.3: Sentence forms attempted but errors predominate, preventing most meaning from coming through; too short to show control of sentence forms.

excluded_error_types.ERR_UNDER_LENGTH: Word count is handled by the backend (warning added to improvements when under 250 words); the LLM must not use this code.
